newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL TAKING U.S. TO WTO FOR TALKS ON CHIPS-PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL TAKING U.S. TO WTO FOR TALKS ON CHIPS-PAPERS.

text.p: South Korea is to take the United States to the World Trade Organisation for bilateral consultation on anti-dumping allegations against Seoul's semiconductor exports, local newspapers reported on Tuesday.

The Korea Times and several other newspapers said in their Wednesday morning editions seen late on Tuesday that it was the second time Seoul had taken Washington to the world trade body for bilateral consultations.
Consultations are currently under way between the two to resolve anti-dumping allegations against South Korean colour television exports to the U.S., they said.
Trade ministry officials were unavailable for comment.
The newspaper reports quoted trade ministry officials as saying the ministry would send a letter to Washington on Wednesday requesting bilateral consultations.
Once the letter is received, the U.S. has 30 days to comply and then the two countries would be given another 30 days to work out their differences, the reports said.

Should these bilateral consultations fail to produce a compromise, South Korea has the option of requesting the formation of a panel comprising three international experts under the dispute settlement body.
The Seoul government reached the decision after the U.S. refused to take two South Korean chipmakers off the list of firms facing annual anti-dumping investigations, they said.

The U.S. Trade Representative's office said last month it would keep Hyundai Electronics Industries Co and LG Semicon Co on the list because there is no clear evidence they will not dump their products in the U.S. market.
Early last month the office imposed anti-dumping margins reported at 0.00 percent on Hyundai and 0.01 percent on LG, following similarly low duties in its two previous rulings in 1996.
